clauses.reason: Treasury implementation authority for Resolution 778 and repaid assets is prospective authority revoked expressly by EO13350; no factual completion date is inferred from a transfer program.

The financial-institution transfer command is conditional on Treasury determinations and directions and is revoked prospectively by EO13350. Receipt of one transfer would not prove every potential transfer completed.
New York Federal Reserve receipt, holding, investment and onward transfers are continuing commands until revoked, with accrued obligations addressed as residuals.

Discharge, good-faith protection and preservation of pre-transfer rights are assessed expressly: protection for transactions already performed can remain accrued, but it supplies no independent command to make new transfers after revocation.
The financial-institution definition serves the transfer/implementation commands and has no independent prospective operation after those commands are revoked.
Treasury rulemaking, redelegation and all-agency implementation duties implement this order and are expressly revoked with it; preserved prior actions and matured duties are residual matters.
The no-private-right clause limits enforcement of this order and is ancillary to the order's implementation; it does not supply an independent ongoing asset-transfer mandate.

Immediate effectiveness and transmittal/publication concern enactment and notice of this order; completed notice is not a current independent obligation. The last prospective authority is expressly revoked effective July 30, 2004, 12:01 a.m. EDT under EO13350 section 10.

savings.reason: EO12817 section 4 gives completed-transfer acquittance, good-faith protection and preservation of pre-transfer rights, debts and claims. EO13350 section 1 saves prior actions/proceedings and matured rights/duties/penalties. Such accrued legal consequences are retained, without asserting a particular transfer occurred; no new transfer, investment, repayment or rulemaking command continues independently under EO12817.

research_rationale: The original complete text has eight sections. OCR conflates sections 1/2 and invents a standalone empty section 8; exact overrides restore the complete inventory. EO13350 expressly revokes EO12817 and section 10 sets July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT, not its July 29 signing date. No unproved occurrence of Treasury determinations, transfers, UN repayments, or exhaustion of asset accounts is used as an earlier end. Section 4 discharge/good-faith protection and preservation of pre-transfer rights remain accrued consequences; the no-private-right provision is ancillary. EO13350 section 1 saves prior actions, pending proceedings and matured rights/duties. Its continuing blocking language is expressly for EO12722/12724, not fresh EO12817 transfer authority. No independent original command survives the express revocation within the bounded evidence. The selected original text is complete on its face and its bytes/provenance are pinned; page-image authentication is not claimed. Searches are accepted only for the bounded contrary-evidence task through the specified cutoff, not as substantive proof of an operative current predicate.
